slides.headline: Stiff, achy hip in the mornings?
slides.sub: Hip osteoarthritis is common, and exercise is usually the first thing to try.

slides.title: Hip OA is very common
slides.body: Osteoarthritis is a common change in the hip joint as we get older. It often shows up as a groin or front-of-hip ache, stiffness after sitting, and trouble putting on socks or shoes.

slides.title: Exercise is first-line care
slides.body: Current guidelines recommend exercise and education as first-line care for hip osteoarthritis, whatever the X-ray shows. Strength and movement can help with pain and daily function for many people.

slides.title: Four moves to start with
slides.body: Sit to stand from a chair, bridges, side-lying leg lifts and step-ups. Two or three sessions a week, building gradually over time, is a reasonable place to begin for most people.

slides.title: Keep walking, adjust the dose
slides.body: Walking, cycling and swimming are usually fine. Some ache during activity is OK if it settles within a day. If it doesn't, shorten the distance or slow the pace rather than stopping.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Hip pain after a fall, being unable to take weight, a hot swollen joint, fever, or pain that wakes you every night and keeps building should be checked by your GP promptly.
